title: Fog in Mesh Topology (Enhanced)
description: This scenario explores fog dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions. The mesh topology ensures connectivity but introduces the risk of outdated information propagation through multi-hop relays.
edge_cases_to_watch: Agents may observe stale route status due to multi-hop relay delays
Messages about bridge closures arrive 1 turn late
Agents must decide whether to trust stale observations from fog-affected peers
Information 'echoes': An agent receives the same stale update via two different mesh paths, incorrectly increasing its confidence in the data
Topology-induced isolation: A fog-impacted agent becomes a bottleneck for routing messages between healthy agents
coordination_challenges: Consensus Latency: Reaching agreement on a route change when the fog-affected agents (a, b) are providing delayed/degraded telemetry
Conflicting Truths: Agent 'c' sees an open route, but Agent 'a' reports it closed; agents must resolve the conflict without direct observation
Bandwidth Congestion: High-priority job updates may be delayed by redundant mesh rerouting during fog-induced uncertainty
Trust Decay: Agents must dynamically weigh the reliability of messages based on the sender's proximity to the fog zone
suggested_agent_strategies: Temporal Weighting: Prioritize recent observations over historical data when calculating route probability
Redundant Verification: For high-priority jobs, require confirmation from at least two distinct mesh paths before rerouting
Conservative Routing: During fog periods, choose paths with higher capacity/redundancy even if they are sub-optimal in distance
Predictive State Estimation: Use Kalman-like filtering to estimate if a route is likely 'open' based on last known status and elapsed turns

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimization of 'dead-end' movements caused by stale data
